flawed_step: The universal claim 'for every n >= 4' fails: self-complementary graphs exist only when n ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4).
counterexample: n = 6. K_6 has C(6,2)=15 edges. If G on 6 vertices has e edges, its complement has 15−e edges. An isomorphism preserves edge count, so e = 15−e, i.e. e = 7.5, which is impossible. Hence no self-complementary graph on 6 vertices exists.
assessment_summary: Counting edges refutes the statement: a self-complementary graph on n vertices needs n(n−1)/2 to be even, which happens only when n ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4). For n=6 there are 15 possible edges, an odd number, so no self-complementary graph exists.
